Physical Description Report: Really filled out this past winter, though reports of this added weight being "bad" are extremely overblown. Quite frankly, he just has a big butt now. Still a little room to fill out in the upper half, but he's pretty close to fully formed. Looks a bit closer to the Jose Ramirez type of build now.
Hit / Mechanics Report: Swings are essentially mirrored from the left and right side. Hands start in a pretty stock position, getting the barrell tipped flat over his shoulder as he gets into his load. There's quite a bit of hand movement involved, though it's been cleaned up a bit over the last year or so. Shows an ability to spray the ball to all fields and to go gap-to-gap. The bat path itself is pretty flat, has had a tendency to get out over his front foot, causing a high groundball rate on his hardest hit balls, though that seems to be something he's working on and has improved on early in 2026. Chase rate has been a bit higher than expected this season, but he's shown plus-plus bat-to-ball skills to help make up for that a bit. Strikeouts may increase a bit at the upper levels but should not be an issue for him. Potentially plus hit tool.
Power/Pitch 1 Report: Plus exit velocities, especially for his age. The aforementioned tendency to hit the ball on the ground has thus far limited his in-game power numbers, but the adjustment to keeping his weight more balanced is already leading to good results. Potentially plus in-game power if he can continue to elevate his hard-hit more often with these adjustments.
Run/Pitch 2 Report: Made's home-to-first times are trending clsoer to above-average than plus speed these days, but he's still a strong runner with the ability to steal bases at a relatively high clip. Could still steal 20+ in MLB at his peak.
Field/Pitch 3 Report: Good actions on the dirt, is at his best when he's attacking the ball and trusting his instincts. Capable of making athletic plays to his right and his left. The routine plays are where you can see some struggles at times, though he only has four errors at this point in the season. The range does seem to be a bit less after the strength gains this winter. Still looks like he could be a good shortstop, but might be a bit more likely to wind up at third base now.
Arm/Pitch 4 Report: Threw a ball 99.9 MPH this season, has a ton of arm strength. The accuracy, especially when he has time can get a little iffy at times. He guides the ball at times, which can cause inaccuracy. Should be able to be cleaned up with reps.
Summary Report: Made is the number one prospect in baseball currently, and has the potential for plus or better tools across the board, with the glove being the most likely to fall short of that level. He should be in MLB in 2027 and will likely be able to make a solid impact right away. One of the best prospects the Brewers have ever had in their system.

Scouting Notes 2:
Draft Report
If you liked the Wilken pick, especially the power that comes with it, then you should also be very excited about the Bitonti pick. Equipped with some of the biggest raw power in the high school class, Bitonti has a sweet looking left handed swing. Like Knoth, he’s young, even for a high schooler, as he won’t turn 18 until mid November. Despite being a pretty good athlete for his size, it’s unlikely he will be able to stick at shortstop. In fact, the Brewers are already planning to have him start at third base. He should be a very strong defender at the hot corner, and he certainly has the arm to handle it as well. The question for Bitonti will come with his hit tool. He does have some holes in his swing presently, and he has struggled with making solid contact on breaking balls. His issues with breaking balls seem to be more aligned with his feel to hit them, as he doesn’t chase them much. This is a good sign. It means he likely just needs to get more comfortable with his bat path against spinners, rather than learning how to recognize them entirely. He crushed fastballs in the prep circuit and should have no issues handling professional velocity. There’s big time, middle of the order upside with Bitonti. Brewers fans will just need to remember to be patient.

Wilken may possess the most raw power of any player in this draft class, hitting multiple balls over 115 MPH this past season. It’s a relatively flat swing, which should allow him to have a decent enough hit tool, though he will likely never hit for a high average. While Wilken’s strikeout numbers aren’t in a great spot, you would think he was striking out at a 30% rate with the way some evaluators have talked about it. In reality it was closer to 18% and he cut down on his whiff rate and chase rate in 2023. If there’s any cause for concern, it probably lies more with the Brewers track record of developing these power over hit profiles.Defensively, scouts are split on whether he can handle third base. He certainly has the arm for it, but the actions and movements do look a bit slow. The Brewers haven’t been shy to play slow movers at third base before though, and his hands seem to be decent enough to handle it.  Despite the concerns about the fit within the organization and their ability to develop him, Wilken is pretty well developed already and he will likely be able to move through the organization relatively quickly.

Like Boeve, Birchard was a player that I was a big fan of during the process and another that just felt like he would end up a Brewer. He was using a slider and changeup as his secondary pitches in the fall, but once he had made it through his season and into the draft league he seemed to have scrapped the changeup in favor of a curveball. The slider and curveball have different shapes and are in different velocity bands. He should be just fine without the changeup. Some think he will end up in the bullpen long term, but I personally do believe he can make it as a starter with his three pitch mix. If he ends up falling back to a bullpen role, it could be a high leverage type of arm and role.

2022 Draft Report'
  Personal favorite of mine in this draft. Really excited that the Brewers got him.
  Believe he was ranked far too low. Upper first round talent.
  Weird setup and load seemed to turn people off, but I don't care about that. He's consistently on time. 
  The high hands actually seem to help his bat path.
  Combination of bat to ball, with his bat speed is not seen anywhere else in this class.
  Extremely low chase rate (9%) and whiff rate.
  In game power has not shown up yet. However, OVER 60% of his batted balls were hit > 95 mph. 
  Along with the exit velos over 95 MPH, he has been up to 113 MPH. He has raw power that he can tap into.
  If I had a nitpick, I think he takes some hittable pitches, because he's so patient. 
  The over abundance of patience is probably fine, because he does not panic when behind in counts and doesn't need to ""shorten up"" to avoid striking out.
  Above average speed, but uses the Brian Roberts stealing technique to a lot of success.
  I bet he will be able to steal double digits in the majors pretty easily, possibly getting to 30+ bases with the likelihood of new rules helping baserunners.
  Defensive actions at short are really good. Glove will stick and could be close to plus.
  Arm strength is a bit of a concern from pundits, but he does a great job of getting his throws off quickly and personally I think there's plenty of zip, I grade it as an above average arm. The quickness of the release should alleviate a lot of that concern anyway though.
  If he has to move off of short to play second, he's likely a 70 grade defender.
  Have a feeling I will be the high guy on Brown for a while. I would've been happy with taking him in the early teens of this draft.The fact they were able to get him so far below slot and use those savings on Misiorowski is a job *really* well done in my opinion."
